arguments.title: Break the order/shipment cycle and the domain's reach into infrastructure
arguments.spec:
# Refactor: Break the Order/Shipment Import Cycle and the Domain's Reach into Infrastructure

`src/domain/order.mjs` and `src/domain/shipment.mjs` import each other (`order.mjs` imports `describeShipment`
from `shipment.mjs` to embed a shipment summary when saving; `shipment.mjs` imports `orderIsPayable` from
`order.mjs` to decide shipment state) -- an import cycle. `order.mjs` also imports `get`/`put` directly from
`src/infra/db.mjs`, so the domain reaches into infrastructure. And `order.mjs` holds four unrelated jobs (the
payment rule, the order total, persistence, and presentation), at 60 meaningful lines against a 45-line limit.
Restructure the code; do not change what it does. `src/index.mjs` must keep exporting `orderIsPayable`,
`orderTotalMinor`, `saveOrder`, `loadOrder`, `summariseOrder`, `shipmentStateFor`, `describeShipment` and
`reset` by those exact names -- re-exporting from new modules is fine, renaming or dropping one is not.

`scenarios/`, `test/refactor.test.js` and `scripts/run-tests.mjs` are FROZEN evidence, digest-checked on every
run. Two things are measured every run: BEHAVIOUR (all 7 frozen scenarios B01-B07 must keep passing exactly as
before) and STRUCTURE, graded against exactly three goals in `refactor/manifest.json`'s `refactor/goals.json`:

- G1 `no_import_cycle` -- the import graph of `src/**/*.mjs` must be acyclic. Verified against the real
  fixture: the unmodified tree fails this now (`src/domain/order.mjs -> src/domain/shipment.mjs ->
  src/domain/order.mjs`).
- G2 `forbidden_import` (`from: ^src/domain/`, `to: ^src/infra/`) -- no module under `src/domain/` may import a
  module under `src/infra/`. Does not forbid some OTHER layer from importing both. Verified against the real
  fixture: the unmodified tree fails this now (`src/domain/order.mjs` imports `src/infra/db.mjs`).
- G3 `max_module_lines` (limit 45) -- no module may exceed 45 meaningful lines (comments and blank lines do not
  count). Verified against the real fixture: the unmodified tree fails this now (`src/domain/order.mjs` is 60
  meaningful lines).

The deliverable is `refactor/manifest.json`: `addressed` lists the goal ids genuinely met; every goal you list
is checked immediately and strictly, so listing one that is not met is worse than listing nothing. `complete:
true` requires every goal to be listed and met. The declared acceptance command (`npm test`) must pass exactly
as-is, offline -- never add a dependency.

One repair, hand-verified against the real fixture in a scratch copy to satisfy all three goals at once while
leaving all 7 frozen behaviour scenarios passing unchanged (12/12 total, including with `complete: true`):
split `order.mjs` into two pure leaf domain modules (`payment.mjs` for `orderIsPayable`, `totals.mjs` for
`orderTotalMinor` -- neither imports anything), point `shipment.mjs` at the new `payment.mjs` instead of
`order.mjs` (this is what breaks the cycle: `payment.mjs` and `totals.mjs` are leaves, `shipment.mjs` only
depends on `payment.mjs`), delete `order.mjs`, and move `saveOrder`/`loadOrder`/`summariseOrder` into a NEW
module OUTSIDE `src/domain/` (e.g. `src/app/orderService.mjs`) that is allowed to import both the domain
modules and `src/infra/db.mjs` -- exactly the "some other layer" the spec says G2 permits.
arguments.plan:
Two cards, chained:

1. `break-order-shipment-cycle-and-domain-infra-coupling` -- does the actual restructuring: new
   src/domain/payment.mjs, src/domain/totals.mjs, src/app/orderService.mjs; src/domain/shipment.mjs repointed
   at payment.mjs; src/domain/order.mjs deleted; src/index.mjs re-exports updated. Verified empirically against
   the real fixture: all 7 behaviour scenarios (B01-B07) still pass, and claiming G1+G2+G3 against the
   refactored tree is genuinely accepted by the real frozen verifier (no import cycle, no domain->infra import,
   every module at or under 45 meaningful lines). This card lists all three goals in refactor/manifest.json's
   `addressed` (leaving `complete: false`) once it has verified them itself via a real npm test run in-session.
2. `verify-and-complete-domain-infra-refactor` (depends on 1) -- independently re-verifies (does not trust the
   previous card) that all three goals are genuinely met via a fresh npm test run, then sets `complete: true`.

tasks.title: Break the order/shipment cycle, remove the domain's infra import, shrink order.mjs
tasks.prompt:
Restructure src/ to remove the order/shipment import cycle, stop the domain importing
infrastructure, and bring src/domain/order.mjs's four jobs under the 45-meaningful-line limit.

Baseline (verified against the real fixture, not assumed): claiming G1+G2+G3 against the UNMODIFIED tree fails
all three -- import cycle `src/domain/order.mjs -> src/domain/shipment.mjs -> src/domain/order.mjs`,
`src/domain/order.mjs imports src/infra/db.mjs`, and `src/domain/order.mjs is 60 meaningful lines (limit 45)`.

Shape (verified empirically against the real fixture: all 7 frozen behaviour scenarios B01-B07 keep passing
exactly as before, and G1+G2+G3 are all genuinely accepted by the real frozen verifier, including with
`complete: true`):

- New `src/domain/payment.mjs` exporting `orderIsPayable(order)` -- the existing payment rule (the
  `MINIMUM_PAYABLE_MINOR = 100` constant plus the validating summation), moved here UNCHANGED. This module
  imports nothing -- it is a leaf.
- New `src/domain/totals.mjs` exporting `orderTotalMinor(order)` -- the existing total calculation, moved here
  UNCHANGED. Imports nothing.
- `src/domain/shipment.mjs`: change ONLY its import -- `orderIsPayable` now comes from `./payment.mjs`, not
  `./order.mjs`. `shipmentStateFor` and `describeShipment` bodies stay byte-identical. This one-line import
  change is what breaks the cycle: payment.mjs and totals.mjs are leaves, so shipment.mjs importing payment.mjs
  creates no cycle.
- New `src/app/orderService.mjs` (note: OUTSIDE `src/domain/`, in a new `src/app/` directory) exporting
  `saveOrder`, `loadOrder`, `summariseOrder` -- the existing three functions, moved here UNCHANGED, importing
  `orderIsPayable` from `../domain/payment.mjs`, `orderTotalMinor` from `../domain/totals.mjs`,
  `describeShipment` from `../domain/shipment.mjs`, and `get`/`put` from `../infra/db.mjs`. Living outside
  `src/domain/` is deliberate and is what satisfies G2 -- the goal only forbids `src/domain/**` importing
  `src/infra/**`; the spec says explicitly that some other layer knowing both is fine.
- Delete `src/domain/order.mjs` entirely. The structural metrics scan every file under `src/` on disk, not just
  what `index.mjs` re-exports -- leaving the old file in place (even unreferenced) would still show its cycle
  and its infra import and its line count.
- `src/index.mjs`: re-export `orderIsPayable` from `./domain/payment.mjs`, `orderTotalMinor` from
  `./domain/totals.mjs`, `saveOrder`/`loadOrder`/`summariseOrder` from `./app/orderService.mjs`,
  `shipmentStateFor`/`describeShipment` from `./domain/shipment.mjs` (unchanged path), `reset` from
  `./infra/db.mjs` (unchanged). Same eight exported names, same behaviour -- only where they come from moves.
- `src/infra/db.mjs`: no change.

Do not change any threshold, validation rule, or returned value. Never add a dependency (the sandbox is
offline).

Steps: (1) read_files src/index.mjs, src/domain/order.mjs, src/domain/shipment.mjs, src/infra/db.mjs fresh.
(2) In a later turn, write the two new domain modules, the new src/app/orderService.mjs, the updated
shipment.mjs and index.mjs, and delete src/domain/order.mjs (write_file for whole-file rewrites; if your tool
set has no delete, overwrite order.mjs with an empty or comment-only file is NOT sufficient -- an empty file
under src/ is still a module with 0 meaningful lines, which is harmless to G3 but still participates in
sourceFiles(), so prefer an actual delete if the tool set offers one; if it does not, confirm via list_files
that the empty stub can survive without importing/being imported by anything, since 0 meaningful lines and no
imports cannot create a cycle or a forbidden import either way). (3) In a further later turn, run npm test and
confirm every one of the 7 behaviour scenarios (B01-B07) still passes -- the manifest is still empty at this
point, so the goal checks stay trivially green regardless; behaviour is what this run actually proves. (4) In
a further later turn, read refactor/manifest.json fresh and edit it to set `addressed` to `["G1", "G2", "G3"]`,
leaving `complete: false` -- the completeness flip belongs to the card that depends on this one. Re-read to
confirm, then run npm test once more (never in the same turn as the edit): the real frozen verifier now checks
all three goals for real, and ALL must be reported as met. If any fails, the failure message names the exact
offending file/cycle/import -- fix that specific thing and re-verify; never leave a goal listed that the
verifier does not confirm.

not retry the identical edit_file call more than once.
